messages.subject: plot function error
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

I integrated my own model into the package. Everything works well except for the plot function. I want to plot the posterior distribution of the hyper parameter, but when I run plot("the hBayesDM object of my model I got") it shows:

Error in plot_aversivelearning_delta(obj = x, fontSize = , ncols = , binSize = ) :
  could not find function "plot_aversivelearning_delta"

Could you think of any causes for this error?

Thank for your time in advance!

Best regards,
Lili

messages.subject: adding new models
messages.body_plain:
Dear hBayesDM developers,

Thanks for this brilliant toolbox. I would like to add new models but I had issues compiling new models.

Therefore, I did a simple test: I created two stan files and corresponding Yaml files with models that are identical to existing ones but with different model names.

I then generated R and python3 codes using the script hBayesDM/commons/generate-codes.sh

All seemed good so far.

Finally I tried to install the R package but I get the error message posted below, where bandit4arm_combLR_lapse* are the names of the files that I have added (identical to the bandit4arm_lapse* files but with a different name).

Any idea of what the problem might be? I have the latest python and hBayseDM version, running on a Mac Os Mojave 10.14.

I would be very grateful for some help!

Best wishes,

Flavia

messages.subject: Re: plot function error
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lili,

It is great to hear you were able to incorporate your model! I am wondering if you added a plotting function to the plotting directory (see:  https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/wiki/Adding-a-new-model-for-a-new-task)?

This specific file is located here on the github repo: https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/blob/master/R/inst/plotting/plot_functions.R

If you add a plotting function with the correct naming scheme there (i.e. "plot_aversivelearning_delta") before running roxygen2::roxygenize(), I think this should fix your problem!

Best,
Nate

messages.subject: Re: adding new models
messages.body_plain:
Hi Flavia,

It seems that DESCRIPTION file does not have information for new R files. In order to solve the issue, you should generate documentation before building or installing the package. Could you try running the following commands?

```
devtools::build()  # In order to build first to make a C++ header file
devtools::document()  # Update DESCRIPTION from R files
devtools::install()
```

Best,
Jaeyeong

messages.subject: drift diffusion model error
messages.body_plain:
Hello Bayesians,

I would like to see if my data fits a drift diffusion model. Attached you will find my data (I have 33 subjects in total, its only an example).
If I run a choiceRT_ddm model using that data, I get the following error:

Stan model 'choiceRT_ddm' does not contain samples.

as well as this error for the initial value in chain 1:

Rejecting initial value:
Chain 1:   Error evaluating the log probability at the initial value.
Chain 1: Exception: validate transformed params: tau[1] is 0.0338836, but must be greater than or equal to 0.1  (in 'model384c763e527d_choiceRT_ddm' at line 44)

I am assuming it might be the Reaction time, but I don't see why?

Further: subjects have two choices in each trial (right vs. left key), their decision is based on a random dot task but additionally we have a feature that predicts the correct choice in each trial perfectly (from a later block on).
Anyone an idea what model I could use or might try?

Thank you so much for your help.

Carina

messages.subject: Re: modify model in HbayesDM package
messages.body_plain:
Hi Lili,

I'm sorry for this very late reply. From next year (2020), we plan to respond in a timely manner.

In step 6, basically you need to write up some codes for generating 'data_list'.

For example, if you check the 'data' block in the Stan code for the 'bandit2arm' task (https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/blob/master/commons/stan_files/bandit2arm_delta.stan), there are five variables that need to be provided by the user: N, T, Tsubj, choice, outcome. In the preprocess function, we need to specify how the five variables are generated from the raw data file (or a data.frame).

Given the similarity of yours and the 'badnti2arm_delta' model, you can start from its template. You can see how we did it for the 'bandit2arm' task: https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/blob/2781155befd2889cafcf6336366f47f4bf392be0/R/R/preprocess_funcs.R#L4

In this code <https://github.com/CCS-Lab/hBayesDM/blob/master/R/R/preprocess_funcs.R>, you can probably use lines 7-11 as they are. 'subjs' are subject IDs, n_subj is the number of subjects, t_subjects is number of trials for each subject, and t_max is the maximum number of trials among all subjects. What's left to be done is how you extract info from the raw file and convert them into the five variables (N, T, Tsubj, choice, outcome).

Hope this helps and let me know if you have any further questions or need more help. Thanks!

Best,
Young
